title: Depth-Bounds for Neural Networks via the Braid Arrangement

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract vs Theorem 4.8 / Theorem 5.2 / Section 7 Conclusion
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract claims 'the first unconditional non-constant lower bound of Omega(log log d) hidden layers ... in general ReLU networks' and that 'arbitrary neural networks require three hidden layers to compute the maximum of 5 numbers', but the paper's actual results (Theorem 4.8, Theorem 5.2) hold only for B_d/B_d^0-conforming networks. The Conclusion states verbatim: 'We established a doubly-logarithmic lower bound under the assumption that breakpoints lie on the braid fan' and cites Bakaev et al. [2025b] showing the maximum of 5 numbers IS computable with 2 hidden layers by general networks — the exact opposite of the abstract's claim. The abstract's 'We completely resolve the open question' is contradicted by the Conclusion's 'remains an open problem'.

Abstract misstates the paper's own results: (1) 'unconditional ... general ReLU networks' vs conforming-only Theorem 4.8; (2) 'arbitrary neural networks require three hidden layers to compute the maximum of 5 numbers' contradicts Bakaev et al. [2025b] (two hidden layers suffice), a result the paper itself cites and relies on in the Conclusion; (3) 'completely resolve'/'settles a long-standing conjecture' contradicted by the Conclusion.

'Classical results by Cybenko [1989] and Hornik [1991] showed that ReLU networks compute exactly the class of continuous piecewise linear (CPWL) functions' is false — Cybenko and Hornik proved universal approximation theorems for sigmoidal networks, not exact ReLU representation. The same exact-representation result is correctly attributed to Arora et al. [2018] two paragraphs later, creating an internal contradiction; the sentence also contradicts its own successor ('establishing an analogous result for exact representations remains an open question').

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction ('Prior work by Montúfar and Bengio [2015]...') and References
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: 'Prior work by Montúfar and Bengio [2015] conjectured a doubly-logarithmic lower bound and provided partial results for dimension three' — no such publication exists (web search finds only Montúfar, Pascanu, Cho, Bengio 2014 on linear regions, an unrelated result with no such conjecture), and the paper's reference list contains no corresponding entry. Dangling fabricated citation supporting a material claim.

The formula dim(F_d(k)) = dim(V_{B_d}(k)) = sum_{i=1}^k binom(d,i) is provably wrong: exact rank computation of the constraint system {alpha_{S,T} : r(T)-r(S)=k+1} gives dim F_d(k) = sum_{i=0}^k binom(d,i) for all tested d=2,3,4 and all k (e.g. d=3,k=1: computed 4 vs printed 3; d=4,k=2: computed 11 vs printed 10). At k=d the printed formula yields 2^d - 1, contradicting Proposition 2.2 (dim = 2^d) and the stated chain V(d) = V_{B_d}. The i=0 term is missing.

Exhaustive computation over all 128 subsets of [7] shows the printed intermediate identity is false: F(146) = -1 (so 146 is not in supp^+(F)), <alpha_{12,bar3}, F> = 0, and the printed right-hand side '<alpha_{12,bar3}, F> - F(146) - F(167)' evaluates to 0, not -2. The printed support claim supp^+(F) subseteq [1,bar23] u 146 u 167 is also false (e.g. F({1,2}) = 2 > 0 with {1,2} outside that set). The correct, verified statement is supp^+(F) subseteq [12,bar3] u {145} u {167} with <alpha_{empty,[7]}, F^+> = <alpha_{12,bar3}, F> - F(145) - F(167) = -2. The final value (-2) and Proposition 6.1's conclusion are correct (lambda_{[7]} = 2 != 0; the pair (F_1,F_2) is conforming on all 5040 maximal chains); the error is confined to the printed computation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Definition 2.1 vs Preliminaries (cones/lineality of the braid fan)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Definition 2.1 includes the hyperplanes x_i = 0 in the braid arrangement B_d, which contradicts the immediately following properties: 'The braid fan has span(1_{[d]}) as lineality space' and the cone description cone(1_{S_1},...,1_{S_k}) + span(1_{[d]}) — impossible for a fan refined by x_i = 0 (not invariant under translation by 1_{[d]}). With the printed definition, B_d would coincide with B_d^0 (binom(d,2)+d = binom(d+1,2) hyperplanes), collapsing the B_d/B_d^0 distinction that Lemma 3.1 and 'dividing out the lineality space of B_d yields B^0_{d-1}' depend on. The braid arrangement must consist only of the binom(d,2) hyperplanes x_i = x_j.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, contributions ('first unconditional lower bound', 'first proof' for dimension four); Abstract
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Introduction claims Section 4 proves the bound 'without any conforming or weight restrictions' (it does not — Theorem 4.8 is conforming-only) and claims 'the first proof' that max{0,x1..x4} is not representable by a B_d^0-conforming network with two hidden layers, contradicting the same section's statement that Hertrich et al. [2023] already proved this via mixed-integer programming and the Conclusion's 'we reprove the tight bound ... of Hertrich et al. [2023]'. The published version of this work (arXiv:2502.09324) states 'We contribute towards resolving...' and scopes all claims to braid-fan-compatible networks.

Subcaption (c) prints 'alpha_{d,bcd} - alpha_{a,abc} = alpha_{empty,bcd} - alpha_{empty,abc}', which is sign-flipped: subtracting the (verified-correct) identities (a) and (b) of the same figure gives alpha_{empty,bcd} - alpha_{empty,abc} = alpha_{a,abc} - alpha_{d,bcd}. Verified by exact computation over all 16 subsets of {a,b,c,d}: printed (c) False, negated left-hand side True. Does not invalidate Lemma 4.4(2) (span membership is sign-invariant) but the printed equation is demonstrably wrong.

summary: Exhaustive strict-mode verification of all 37 snippets found multiple high-confidence, erratum-level errors concentrated in the framing sections, plus three verified technical errors. (1) The Abstract and Introduction systematically overstate the results: they claim an 'unconditional' Omega(log log d) depth lower bound for GENERAL ReLU networks and that 'arbitrary neural networks require three hidden layers to compute the maximum of 5 numbers', while the paper's actual theorems (4.8, 5.2) hold only for braid-fan(B_d^0)-conforming networks — and the paper's own Introduction and Conclusion cite Bakaev et al. [2025b] showing 2 hidden layers suffice for the maximum of 5 numbers in general networks, directly contradicting the abstract. The 'first proof' claim for the dimension-four result contradicts the Conclusion's 'we reprove the tight bound of Hertrich et al. [2023]'. (2) The Introduction misattributes the exact CPWL-representation theorem to Cybenko [1989] and Hornik [1991] (who proved universal approximation for sigmoidal networks), contradicting its own later correct attribution to Arora et al. [2018], and cites a nonexistent 'Montúfar and Bengio [2015]' absent from the reference list. (3) Technical errors verified by exact computation: Proposition 2.3's dimension formula sum_{i=1}^k binom(d,i) is wrong (must be sum_{i=0}^k; the printed formula contradicts dim V_{B_d} = 2^d at k=d); the Proposition 6.1 proof sketch's identity '<alpha_{12,bar3},F> - F(146) - F(167) = -2' evaluates to 0 as printed (F(146) = -1; correct version uses F(145) and sublattice [12,bar3] in the support claim — the -2 endpoint and the proposition's conclusion are otherwise correct); Figure 2(c)'s printed alpha-identity is sign-flipped relative to the verified identities (a) and (b). The underlying mathematics of Sections 3-6 (recurrence k -> k^2+k, counting step, Theorem 4.8 arithmetic, the rank-(3,2) maxout construction, conformity of (F_1,F_2) on all 5040 maximal chains) verified correct. Verdict: NEEDS_CORRECTION — the abstract/introduction claims require rewriting to match the proven conforming-network scope, the fabricated citation must be removed, and the three technical misprints corrected.
